issues.description: README diverges from things_advanced.py example (uses bounded_stream but not content_length)
issues.detail: The README JSONTranslator was changed to use req.bounded_stream.read(), but the PR description says things_advanced.py should add req.content_length to req.stream.read(). The actual diff in examples/things_advanced.py only switches to bounded_stream without passing content_length, contradicting the stated intent. README and example should match consistently.

issues.description: FAQ example mishandles Content-Length=1 with empty body — assertion may not match real behavior
issues.detail: The PostTest reads req.content_length bytes from req.stream when Content-Length is 1 but body is empty. req.stream.read(1) on an empty/short body may return b'' or block depending on the WSGI server. Asserting HTTP_400 here is fragile and may not reliably document the intended behavior across implementations.

issues.description: Test does not verify the actual fix — empty body with Content-Length:1 succeeds via bounded_stream regardless
issues.detail: resp4 expects 400 because bounded_stream.read() returns b'' for an empty body even when Content-Length:1. But this also happened before the change with req.stream.read() in many test setups. The test does not clearly demonstrate the bug being fixed and may pass for incidental reasons.

issues.description: FAQ code example missing blank lines between top-level definitions (PEP 8)
issues.detail: The FAQ snippet has the PostTest class followed immediately by @pytest.fixture without two blank lines, and uses non-idiomatic assert syntax `assert(result.status == ...)` with parentheses. Minor style issues that propagate into user-facing docs.

issues.description: StorageError.handle signature changed in README without explanation
issues.detail: The handler signature changed from (ex, req, resp, params) to (req, resp, ex, params). While this matches Falcon's current error handler convention, the change is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose of adding POST tests, and may confuse readers comparing against older docs.

issues.description: Trailing comma in single-element tuple in FAQ doc example is odd
issues.detail: `headers = [('Content-Length', '1'),]` is a list, not a tuple, so the trailing comma is just style. More importantly, the simulate_post headers param is documented as a dict elsewhere in the codebase; using a list of tuples here is inconsistent with the test in tests/test_examples.py which uses a dict.

review.summary: PR adds POST tests for the things_advanced example and switches the example to use req.bounded_stream.read(). The main concerns are: (1) the README snippet and the example diverge from the PR description's stated intent of adding content_length to the read call; (2) the new test may not actually exercise the bug being fixed since bounded_stream returns empty for missing bodies regardless of Content-Length; (3) the FAQ example has minor style and consistency issues with the rest of the test suite. Unrelated cosmetic changes in README (handler signature reordering, code_to_http_status) expand the diff scope.
